title: Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo - Novatech
summary: AE and SE demoed Redwood's hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, Console and Optimize features. Focus: e-commerce search relevance, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot next steps (trial keys, benchmark scripts, pricing and security docs).
next_steps: Maya to send pricing and perf deck and pilot proposal
Derek to share benchmark scripts and sample rerank prompts
Priya to provide sample query logs and success criteria
action_items: Maya Chen - send pricing, perf slides, and SOC2 summary - due 2025-11-25
Derek Alvarez - share benchmark scripts (python + curl) and example dataset - due 2025-11-24
Priya Singh - export 24h of search query logs and sample product metadata - due 2025-11-22
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. We also have Derek, our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:07] Jason Park: Hey, Jason here, head of search at Novatech. Priya and Evan are with me.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hi all.
[00:15] Derek Alvarez: Hi, Derek. I'll be doing the technical part of the demo.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda: quick qual, then live demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, console view, Optimize recommendations, Q&A, next steps.
[00:28] Evan Morales: Sounds good. We're mostly focused on search relevance for e-comm, lots of long tail queries and synonyms. Current stack is Elastic on-prem with some custom reranking.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Got it. Quick qual: what's SLA and latency expectations?
[00:42] Jason Park: We target p95 under 200ms for search page loads, obviously token generation is lower priority but rerank should be fast.
[00:49] Priya Singh: Cost is big too - we can't have per-request costs explode. We want to see improvement in click-through and conversion.
[00:55] Derek Alvarez: Perfect. A couple quick follow-ups: are you doing vector store externally (we see Pinecone, Milvus, etc) or embedding store inside Elastic?
[01:03] Jason Park: We currently store embeddings in Elastic (vectors field) but maintenance is annoying. Open to hosted vector DBs or Redwood-managed approach.
[01:11] Maya Chen: OK. We'll demo the hosted embeddings endpoint for generating vectors and then rerank which takes the original query + candidate doc snippets and returns a reorder. We'll also show how Console metrics tie to Optimize recommendations to reduce cost.
[01:23] Derek Alvarez: Jumping into the demo - I'm in the Redwood Console. On the left is the API playground. First, embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-emb-small, payload: text array. It returns float vectors; note some noise in naming in the transcript, the model name in UI is redwood-embed-1 but API alias works.
[01:39] [01:40] Derek Alvarez: I'll generate embeddings for a product title and a couple descriptions. Response back in ~120ms from our hosted US-west region.
[01:46] Priya Singh: That's quick. What about batching?
[01:49] Derek Alvarez: We support batching and automatic concurrent requests to maximize throughput. In Console Optimize tab you can set batching window and target latency.
[01:56] [02:00] Derek Alvarez: Next, rerank endpoint. POST /v1/rerank expects query + list of candidates. It runs a lightweight cross-encoder style rerank model trained for relevance signals. It returns scores and a new order. Here's an example with 10 candidates. Latency p95 is ~85ms on this demo config.
[02:16] Evan Morales: Is rerank doing embeddings + cross attention? How do you keep it cheap?
[02:20] Derek Alvarez: Good question - it's a hybrid. We do a cheap embedding similarity filter to narrow candidates then run a small cross-encoder for final scoring. This reduces cost and keeps latency low. The runtime supports quantized kernels and KV/cache optimizations for the cross-encoder.
[02:33] Jason Park: Do you support streaming rerank or partial results?
[02:37] Derek Alvarez: Rerank is sync - we return final scores; embeddings endpoint is async-friendly and you can save vectors client-side or via our managed vector store.
[02:44] [03:00] Maya Chen: Let's look at a real-world flow: ingest pipeline - we showed a demo connector that extracts product metadata, computes embeddings via the hosted API, and writes them to a managed vector index. Then search flow is query -> kNN from index -> rerank top K -> present results.
[03:18] Priya Singh: How do you handle freshness? We have frequent catalog updates and price changes.
[03:23] Derek Alvarez: You can set TTLs on vectors or run incremental re-embeds. Console has a jobs page where you can schedule re-embedding, or you can stream updates via our API.
[03:30] Priya Singh: Ok. Security: we need SSO, SAML, VPC peering options, and SOC2/ISO docs. Any on-prem option?
[03:38] Maya Chen: Yes - hosted API with optional Private deployment for full isolation. We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integrations. We'll share the SOC2 summary and the architecture doc.
[03:47] Evan Morales: Data retention - do you store raw queries or PII?
[03:50] Derek Alvarez: By default we retain logs for 30 days but you can configure retention or disable retention for sensitive fields; private deploy allows you to keep logs on your side. We'll send the exact policy doc.
[04:00] [04:20] Derek Alvarez: Back to the Console: Optimize tab - it runs workload analysis. For a given route you can see token breakdown, per-request cost, and suggestions: reduce context window, enable caching of common query prefixes, and apply a cheaper embedding model for long-tail. We can auto-generate quantization recommendations too.
[04:36] Jason Park: Can Optimize recommend different embed model for bulk ingestion vs rerank?
[04:39] Derek Alvarez: Yes - it shows separate profiles per route and suggests using redwood-embed-small for indexing and larger cross-encoder for rerank only. You can pin model versions per route.
[04:48] Priya Singh: How do we evaluate quality improvements? We need clear metrics tied to CTR and revenue lift.
[04:52] Maya Chen: We'll help design an eval set from your query logs and measure baseline vs rerank. Our rollout supports canary and A/B tests with traffic split and automatic rollback.
[05:02] [05:30] Evan Morales: What's the expected unit cost if we run rerank on top of kNN? Ballpark per-100k queries?
[05:36] Maya Chen: Ballpark depends on model sizes and batching. For reference, a small embedding call plus a small rerank cross-encoder, at moderate batching, would be X cents per request - we'll include concrete numbers in the pricing deck.
[05:46] Derek Alvarez: Also note caching: many searches are repeated; prefix caching can reduce calls substantially. In Demo logs we saw 40% reduction in calls for top 5 queries.
[05:58] [06:20] Priya Singh: Can we run a short pilot with 10k queries to validate p95 and CTR?
[06:23] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We typically do a 1-week pilot with a small data slice, benchmarking script, and success criteria. We'll provide trial API keys and a sandbox vector index.
[06:33] Jason Park: What about integration complexity - do we need to change our ES pipeline a lot?
[06:36] Derek Alvarez: Minimal. You can keep ES as primary and use Redis/Lucene kNN or our managed vector store for nearest-neighbor; the rerank call is just an HTTP request. We have example connectors.
[06:48] [07:00] Derek Alvarez: I'll run a quick live rerank example using Novatech sample product text. (typing) Here's the original top-5 results, and here's rerank output - you can see the result that matches the query intent moved to top 1.
[07:18] Priya Singh: Nice, that looks promising though we'll need to test at scale.
[07:22] Evan Morales: Are there rate limits?
[07:24] Maya Chen: Hosted API has rate limits per account; Dedicated customers can get higher reserved throughput. We can propose reserved capacity if your volume needs it.
[07:30] Jason Park: Any regulator concerns - data residency in EU?
[07:33] Maya Chen: We have regions and private deployment options for data residency. We can discuss specific compliance needs in the security doc.
[07:40] [08:00] Derek Alvarez: Quick note on instrumentation: Console exposes per-route latency histograms, token counts, and a trace to correlate requests. You can export metrics to Datadog or Prometheus.
[08:10] Priya Singh: Great. Can Optimize detect regressions after a model change?
[08:14] Derek Alvarez: Yes - quality monitoring ties to eval sets. You get alerts on regressions for defined prompts with rollout gating.
[08:21] Maya Chen: Wrapping up - recap of next steps: we'll send pricing and perf deck, SOC2/security docs, example benchmark scripts; Priya will share logs; schedule pilot kickoff.
[08:35] Evan Morales: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with materials and proposed dates.
[08:45] [END]
